sepsis.who.unknown: Community-acquired sepsis of unknown source: cefotaxime or ceftriaxone combined with amikacin or gentamicin; 7 days. Once the source is found, follow the infection-specific guidance.
sepsis.ssc.time_shock: Septic shock: give antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour of recognition.
sepsis.ssc.time_no_shock: No shock: investigate rapidly; if concern for infection persists, give antimicrobials within 3 hours.
sepsis.who.shock_dose: Dose adjustments may be required in septic shock; listed doses are for normal renal and hepatic function.
sepsis.ssc.mrsa: High MRSA risk: empiric MRSA coverage is recommended. The source table names no agent in this row; adding one is an expert decision.
sepsis.ssc.mdr: High risk of resistant organisms: two agents with Gram-negative coverage are suggested (this regimen already has two). Amikacin remains active against many ESBL producers.
sepsis.note.icu: Guidelines give no separate intensive care regimen; the table covers community-acquired sepsis. Hospital-acquired sepsis needs local resistance data and expert advice.
syndrome.sepsis_unknown.aliases: unknown, sepsis, septic shock, no source, unclear focus, intensive care, ICU

guideline.jsscg-2024.name: J-SSCG 2024 (Japan)

question.sepsis_acquisition.label: Onset
question.sepsis_3gcr_risk.label: Risk of third-generation cephalosporin resistance
sepsis.swab.low: Low resistance risk, unknown source: a third-generation cephalosporin. Alternatives: piperacillin-tazobactam, or cefuroxime with ciprofloxacin or an aminoglycoside. 7 days; aminoglycoside for two days at most.
sepsis.swab.increased: Increased resistance risk: a cephalosporin with an aminoglycoside, or a carbapenem, are equivalent (without renal insufficiency). Aminoglycoside for two days at most.
sepsis.swab.high: Resistant organism cultured in the prior year: meropenem or imipenem preferred.
sepsis.swab.no_double: This guideline does not step up for shock or intensive care and recommends against routine double active therapy. It has no MRSA branch (low Dutch MRSA rate).
sepsis.jsscg.community: Community-acquired, unknown source: ceftriaxone. 7 days. If meningitis is possible, follow the meningitis guidance.
sepsis.jsscg.healthcare: Healthcare-associated (P. aeruginosa and MRSA possible): cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam or meropenem, with vancomycin. 7 days.
sepsis.jsscg.carbapenem: A carbapenem is chosen only when an organism susceptible to carbapenems alone is expected (ESBL producers, resistant Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter).
sepsis.s3.com_sepsis: Community-acquired sepsis, unknown source: piperacillin-tazobactam or cefotaxime.
sepsis.s3.com_shock: Community-acquired septic shock: piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime or meropenem.
sepsis.s3.nos_shock: Hospital-acquired septic shock: piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime or meropenem, with linezolid.
sepsis.s3.mrsa: MRSA risk: add linezolid; vancomycin with level monitoring is the alternative.
sepsis.s3.mrgn: Septic shock with risk of resistant Gram-negatives: add ciprofloxacin; meropenem preferred as the beta-lactam.
sepsis.s3.consensus: This table is expert consensus and gives no doses or duration; doses and the 7 day duration come from other guidelines. Adapt to local resistance data.
